headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; ms-swift can write/egress sensitive artifacts while Plane accepts file uploads and broad network exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and emit logs/configuration outputs, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. There is no documented shared channel or parser bridge between them, so prompt-injection risk is limited to unusual manual transfer of content rather than a default automated pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ms-swift output into Plane issue text or file uploads
IF Plane content is later re-ingested by ms-swift as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste model output into task descriptions without review
Strip instruction-like text from uploaded files
Use a fixed template for handoffs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift explicitly handles hub_token and sdk-token and can write files, logs, and training outputs; Plane accepts file uploads and has broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, sensitive artifacts can be copied from ms-swift into Plane and then exposed through Plane's networked workflows, creating a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF ms-swift writes secrets or checkpoints into files that are uploaded into Plane
IF Plane users or integrations can access uploaded attachments or linked content
mitigations: Store secrets outside ms-swift working directories
Review and redact uploads before placing them in Plane
Restrict Plane attachment visibility
Rotate any token that may have been written to disk
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has filesystem write and shell/subprocess capabilities, while Plane has no filesystem write but does support broad network egress and multiple instances. They do not obviously contend for the same mutable resource, so direct write-write conflict is not documented; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory or mounted volume
IF Plane file uploads are synchronized back into ms-swift's workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable shared mounts between runtimes
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Lock any shared artifact before handoff
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate logs, evaluation outputs, and configuration data, and Plane is an issue/task system that can store notes and files. If ms-swift output is treated as authoritative and then copied into Plane tasks or schedules without verification, errors can cascade across work products; Plane's workflow role makes this plausible in default use.
conditions: IF ms-swift-generated text is pasted into Plane as task content or status updates
IF Plane automation acts on those entries without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from model output
Mark AI-generated content in task titles or notes
Cross-check facts against source documents
Limit Plane automations on imported text
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub_token and sdk-token and touches datasets, checkpoints, and evaluation outputs, while Plane stores issues, files, notes, and roadmaps with broad network egress. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so the compliance concern is retention and handling of sensitive operational data rather than a proven regulatory breach.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential data is stored in Plane attachments or notes
IF ms-swift artifacts containing secrets are retained in Plane beyond the approved retention window
mitigations: Classify data before uploading to Plane
Set short retention for sensitive tasks
Remove secrets from ms-swift outputs before transfer
Restrict access to sensitive projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
